DNSquachWatch v1.8.2 — ST7789-80MHz, based on SquachWatch v1.35.0.

Display and microSD now use separate SPI controllers. microSD owns HSPI; resistive touch uses software SPI on its original pins while retaining the existing sampling, filtering, rotation and calibration. Capacitive touch remains on I2C. DNSP detection, labels, research, security, accessibility and upstream features remain.

A read-only diagnostic passed cold boot, two RST cycles and repeated root/guide reads on the affected Lerdisk card after controller separation. The full v1.8.2 receiver image still needs hardware verification for touch, radios, writes, backup and Safe Shutdown; this does not claim compatibility with every card.

The app image is 1,948,912 bytes, only 96 bytes larger than v1.8.1, with 17,168 bytes free in the existing slot. Static RAM is 124,352 bytes (+40). ST7789 compilation, native regressions, touch transport and SD adapter tests, desktop UI/banded checks, version/partition checks and image signature verification passed.

Keep existing DNSP Content/v1.5. No ESP32 erase or card reformat is required. The kit includes all four flashing binaries; serial is 115200 baud. Normal firmware card writes are enabled. ILI9341 receiver support remains removed; DNSP uses those boards for the separate simulation project and gifts ST7789 boards with both microUSB and USB-C ports.
